title: Collection List L04-L05 native evidence summary

l04_filter.dependency_evidence: l04-filter-dependencies.json records zero Test/value controls while no filter field is selected; dependent controls are hidden as intended.
limits: All category values in the fixture are Accessibility; no mixed-category positive result is proven.
No numeric/date filter schema is represented.
Arbitrary values and all boolean aliases are not exhaustive.

l05_pagination.route_caveat: The preview route may retain a later page number during native navigation. These receipts prove recorded counts and observed titles only; they do not independently prove first-page/reset state unless titles or aria-current establish it.

evidence.interpretation: per=0 is treated as disabled because renderer requires per > 0; limit 3 remains active.
UI clamps the nonnegative Unit control to 0; renderer then leaves per disabled and limit 3 remains active.
raw decimal persists across reload, while renderer parseInt floors it to 2 for slicing/page count.

The first-to-next transition advances by the effective integer size (2) with no dropped items, while the control still displays/persists 2.5; this is additional evidence of the decimal UI/compiler inconsistency.
large positive integer-like value leaves all 18 published items on one page.

source_analysis.control_definition: app/src/core/index.ts:575-584 defines per/limit as unit controls with units [''], no integer flag, and the shared UnitCtl defaults to min 0 and step any.
source_analysis.ui_validation: app/src/ui/inspector/Controls.tsx:164-203 clamps nonnegative values but allows decimals when integer is not set.
source_analysis.renderer: app/src/core/index.ts:4665-4669 and 5030-5036 use parseInt and per > 0, so pagination is integer-only and decimals are silently truncated.
source_analysis.classification: 0 and negative values behave as the existing disabled/limit precedence policy; decimal persistence versus integer-only rendering is a real UI/compiler contract inconsistency.

minimal_options: Mark per and limit integer-aware in their controls while retaining zero as the disabled value, then add native coverage for decimal entry and reload.
Alternatively reject decimal drafts explicitly; do not silently persist a decimal that the renderer truncates.

limits: Representative gap/alignment values and resets only; arbitrary spacing and all shared style controls remain open.

evidence.proof: id qa-list-native, class qa-list-proof, outline rgb(21,85,119) solid 2px
display:none at the hidden breakpoint while 18 DOM items remain retained

l08_advanced_visibility_condition_follow.condition_semantics: Source review indicates a List node condition is evaluated before its repeat loop against the selected source preview item; it controls whole-list visibility, not per-item filtering. The earlier equality receipts cannot validate this behavior because the Value input uses onChange and the automation did not commit the typed value. Per-item conditions require a repeated child/card descendant.
limits: The earlier is=1 and is=0 equality receipts are rejected probes because the Value input remained blank after fill+Tab; they provide no condition result evidence.
The committed Accessibility/Design cases cover category positive/negative whole-list visibility only; boolean, nested child, blank/nonempty, and legacy-invalid condition cases remain open.
No per-item child/card condition matrix is recorded.
